rule: No cross-theme duplicate symbols: a ticker holds at most ONE company row across all themes; secondary exposure goes in node descriptions or events
learnedFrom: PR #1 fusion - verifier killed MSFT and NVDA rows double-counted with agi-infrastructure

rule: Verify every contract/PPA/round date against the PRIMARY source release, not aggregator coverage - press cycles reuse old announcements
learnedFrom: PR #1 fusion - Air Liquide ITER contract was misdated by NINE YEARS (2015 coverage of a different contract vs the 2014-05-22 release)

rule: Private companies NEVER get company rows - they live in node descriptions and as event actors; if honest public pure-plays do not exist, a mostly-private vertical with few company rows IS the correct answer
learnedFrom: PR #1 fusion - CFS/Helion/TAE/Tokamak Energy are all private; padding rejected by design

rule: Timeline claims must reflect the CURRENT schedule, not the announcement-day schedule - re-verify roadmap dates within the session, and prefer conservative phrasing ('attempt to follow') over specific quarters no source commits to
learnedFrom: PR #1 fusion - SPARC 'operations 2026' was stale; first plasma had slipped to 2027 with construction ~75% complete

rule: Sector boundaries are hard walls: adjacent-but-different tech (fission vs fusion, HALEU vs tritium) is a KILL, and dual-exposure companies must disclose the overlap in their description to avoid double-counting across verticals
learnedFrom: PR #1 fusion - ASPI's Quantum Leap Energy is primarily a fission fuels venture; sector verifier required explicit disclosure

rule: Node ids referenced by companies/events MUST be cross-checked against the nodes actually authored - parallel author lanes drift (fus-offtake-buyers vs fus-offtake-ppas); reconcile refs before the content build
learnedFrom: PR #1 fusion - 11 dangling node refs across 3 companies and 8 events, caught by the world-radar integrity test

rule: No investment-advice-adjacent phrasing in content ('most investable', 'public-market entry points') - describe exposure and evidence, never attractiveness
learnedFrom: PR #1 fusion - two node descriptions rewritten by the facts verifier under the no-advice rule

rule: Funding-round actors: never headline an investor as 'lead' unless the primary release designates one; list named participants as the release words them
learnedFrom: PR #1 fusion - Helion Series F has no designated lead; SoftBank wrongly headlined

rule: Small/mid-cap company rows require a dated, matchable backing event (government or hyperscaler actor) - the content coherence tests enforce it, so author the backing event WITH the company row
learnedFrom: PR #1 fusion - Furukawa row stands because the GBP 70M UK STEP contract satisfies the backing rule
